v19.description: A Button without `variant` is `default`: filled. The main action stands out from the outlined one.

v20.description: A Button without `emphasis` renders `medium`: outlined. ods-migrate renames `variant` to `emphasis` and drops `medium`, the default, so both buttons look the same.

alternative.effect: The codemod adds `emphasis="high"` to every Button that has neither `variant` nor `emphasis`, turns a computed `variant={ v }` into `emphasis={ v ?? 'high' }`, and keeps an explicit `emphasis="medium"` instead of dropping it, so that every migrated Button says its emphasis.

choices.title: Message without variant

v19.description: A Message without `variant` is `default`: a tinted background.

v20.description: A Message without `emphasis` renders `medium`. ods-migrate leaves it without `emphasis`.

alternative.effect: The codemod adds `emphasis="high"` to every Message that has neither `variant` nor `emphasis`, turns a computed `variant={ v }` into `emphasis={ v ?? 'high' }`, and keeps an explicit `emphasis="medium"` instead of dropping it.

choices.renderingNote: `high` is the closest v20 emphasis to the v19 `default`, not the same rendering: v19 had a stronger tint and a dark border and text, see the computed styles below.

choices.title: Card without color

v19.description: A Card without `color` is `primary`: a coloured border.

v20.description: A Card without `status` is `neutral`: a grey border. ods-migrate leaves it as is.

alternative.effect: The codemod adds `status="accent"` to every Card that has neither `color` nor `status`.

choices.renderingNote: The v19 look keeps a coloured border, not the v19 blue: `accent` is navy in the Aluminium theme. To get the v19 blue back as well, load `@ovhcloud/ods-themes/blue-jeans/css` instead of `@ovhcloud/ods-themes/default/css` (one theme only: the last one loaded wins): ods-migrate never changes the theme.

choices.title: Badge color="primary"

v19.description: A `primary` Badge is filled: white text on the primary colour.

v20.description: `primary` becomes `accent`, whose default `medium` emphasis is subtle: a light background with a border.

alternative.effect: The codemod and the ESLint fix add `emphasis="high"` next to `status="accent"` when the v19 value is `primary` (a literal or `BADGE_COLOR.primary`). A computed value is only renamed.

choices.renderingNote: The v19 look keeps a filled badge, not the v19 blue: `accent` is navy in the Aluminium theme.

choices.title: Divider color="neutral"

v19.description: A `neutral` Divider is a dark grey line (`--ods-color-neutral-700`).

v20.description: The `color` prop is removed: every Divider is the light default line. ods-migrate removes the prop.

alternative.effect: The codemod and the ESLint fix remove `color="neutral"` and add an inline `style` that paints the v19 grey. If the Divider already has a `style`, they leave a TODO(ods-v20) marker asking to merge it by hand.

choices.renderingNote: The grey that ods-migrate writes (`--ods-semantic-color-interaction-neutral-hover`, #666) is a little lighter than the v19 one (#4d4d4d, now `--ods-palette-gray-700`, which no semantic token of the line role carries).

choices.title: Spinner color="neutral"

v20.description: The `color` prop is removed: every Spinner takes the accent colour. ods-migrate removes the prop.

alternative.effect: The codemod and the ESLint fix remove `color="neutral"` and add an inline `style` that paints the v19 grey. If the Spinner already has a `style`, they leave a TODO(ods-v20) marker asking to merge it by hand.

choices.renderingNote: The grey that ods-migrate writes (`--ods-semantic-color-surface-neutral`, #757575 in Aluminium) is the closest to the v19 one (#808080); the guide's `content-neutral` is darker (#666666).

choices.title: Page and panel background

v19.description: `--ods-theme-background-color` is white: the page and the panels on it are white.

v20.description: Aluminium has a grey page. ods-migrate maps the token to `surface-page` (grey) where it is declared on `html`, `body` or `:root`, and to `surface-raised` (white) everywhere else.

alternative.effect: ods-migrate maps `--ods-theme-background-color` to `--ods-semantic-color-surface-raised` (white) everywhere, `html`, `body` and `:root` included.

choices.renderingNote: The page and the panel are the integrator's own markup; their colours are the real tokens of both themes.

v19.snippet:
<Button size="xs" variant="outline">Extra small</Button>
<Button size="sm" variant="outline">Small</Button>
<Button variant="outline">Medium</Button>
v19.description: The radius follows the size: 2px, 4px, 8px (a fraction of the container radius).

v20.description: Every size is 4px, the radius of the inputs next to it.

alternative.effect: ods-migrate writes the CSS below into your v19-look stylesheet (its path is under “Your config”). Import it once, after the ODS theme, and outside any CSS @layer: the ODS theme is not in a layer, so a rule inside one always loses to it. It sets the three component tokens on the Button itself, where ODS declares them (a `:root` override would lose).

v19.description: The outer corners are half the container radius: 4px.

v20.description: The outer corners take the whole container radius: 8px, like Card.

alternative.effect: ods-migrate writes the CSS below into your v19-look stylesheet (its path is under “Your config”). Import it once, after the ODS theme, and outside any CSS @layer: the ODS theme is not in a layer, so a rule inside one always loses to it.

v19.description: A rounded rectangle: half the container radius, 4px.

v20.description: A pill (`--ods-semantic-size-radius-full`), with a 1px border in the medium emphasis.

alternative.effect: ods-migrate writes the CSS below into your v19-look stylesheet (its path is under “Your config”). Import it once, after the ODS theme, and outside any CSS @layer: the ODS theme is not in a layer, so a rule inside one always loses to it. Only the corners come back: the v20 border stays.

choices.title: Form field width

v19.description: No default width: a field inside a FormField stretches to its width, Select and Combobox fill their container.

v20.description: Every form field is 280px wide by default, capped at 100% of its container.

alternative.effect: ods-migrate writes the CSS below into your v19-look stylesheet (its path is under “Your config”). Import it once, after the ODS theme, and outside any CSS @layer: the ODS theme is not in a layer, so a rule inside one always loses to it. It gives the field roots back their v19 width. Datepicker is not covered: its width is set on `DatepickerControl`, whose element has no `data-ods`: pass a `className` to `DatepickerControl`.

choices.renderingNote: This v20 change is not final yet: the v20 rendering is a preview, drawn with the v19 colours. Only Input, Select and Textarea are rendered.

choices.title: Font family name

v19.description: ODS 19 declares its font as 'Source Sans Pro' (the files are already Source Sans 3).

v20.description: ODS 20 declares the same files as 'Source Sans 3', with no alias. ods-migrate renames the family and the ODS font asset paths.

alternative.effect: ods-migrate writes the CSS below into your v19-look stylesheet (its path is under “Your config”); import it once, after the ODS theme, and outside any CSS @layer. It puts 'Source Sans Pro' first in the body and heading font tokens. ODS 20 no longer declares that font: host it yourself, or the stack falls back to 'Source Sans 3'. ods-migrate renames the ODS font asset paths in both cases.

choices.renderingNote: The font files did not change between 19 and 20: the three renderings are identical. The choice matters only to an app that loads its own 'Source Sans Pro' (for example @fontsource/source-sans-pro).
